course_name_original: Tecnologías y Paradigmas de la Programación
prerequisites: Programming courses from the first year (Introduction to Programming, Programming Methodology) that allow students to design and develop correct programs in the object-oriented paradigm.
Computability from the first semester of the second year to understand the theoretical foundations of computation and especially computational logic.

learning_outcomes.text: Analyze, design, build and maintain applications robustly, securely, and efficiently, choosing the most appropriate programming paradigm and languages.
Know and be able to apply good software design and implementation practices in order to mitigate and prevent software errors.
Know and be able to apply error control mechanisms at runtime.
Know the security mechanisms in the studied programming paradigms.
Develop an application according to given problem specifications, ensuring the security conditions of the process and environment.
Know the mechanisms for evaluating software performance.
Evaluate the performance of a software development based on the paradigm, language, and environment.
Know the logic and functional programming paradigms.
Know the formal bases of logic and functional programming.
Develop a solution based on logic programming for a given problem specification.
Develop a solution based on functional programming for a given problem specification.
Know what a deductive database is.
Know the concept of a design pattern.
Apply pattern-based design to a given problem specification.
Evaluate the programming paradigm as well as the appropriate language for a given program specification.
Select the programming paradigm as well as the appropriate language for a given program specification.
Understand and apply the fundamental principles and basic techniques of real-time programming, extending from OO paradigm concepts to concurrency and event-oriented programming.

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final theory grade (NotaT) is calculated as the maximum of each part's grades (partial and final exams), weighted proportionally: NotaT = max(10, max(ExT1, ExFT1) * 0.20 + max(ExT2, ExFT2) * 0.30 + max(ExT3, ExFT3) * 0.30 + max(ExT4, ExFT4) * 0.20 + PartT). Similarly for the final practical grade (NotaP). To pass, a minimum score of 4 in both theory and practical blocks is required; the final grade is NotaT * 0.4 + NotaP * 0.6. If minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. In extraordinary calls, a single theoretical exam (ExT) and a single practical exam (ExP) are conducted; previously approved blocks (grade >= 5) from the ordinary call are preserved, and a minimum of 4 in both parts is required.
